question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: In the corner of the estate, behind the crumbling wall, lived an old gardener whom the children called Uncle Hari, though no one now remembered his real name.

A. His hands, however, were the most remarkable thing about him — rough as bark, yet gentle enough to coax the shyest seedling into bloom.

B. Upon his head he always wore a faded red turban, tied loosely, with one end left hanging over his shoulder.

C. Below this weathered face, a coarse cotton kurta hung upon his stooped shoulders, patched so many times that its first colour could no longer be guessed.

D. Beneath its folds, his face was burnt to the colour of old copper by fifty summers in the sun, deep lines crossing from eye to greying beard.

S2: It was said that no flower in the whole district dared to wilt under his care.
solution_text:
The correct answer is B, D, C, A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A head-to-toe physical description that moves downward from turban to hands.

• B (opens the description right after S1 introduces the gardener, starting at the top with the turban on his head) → D ('Beneath its folds' points back to the turban named in B and moves the description down to his face) → C ('Below this weathered face' continues the downward sweep from D to his kurta and shoulders) → A ('however' signals a contrast and shifts to his hands, the final and most remarkable feature, leading into S2's mention of his care for flowers)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• In physical-description passages, look for phrases like 'beneath', 'below this' or 'upon his head' — they signal the fixed top-to-bottom order of the description.

 

NOTE

• Any order that separates the turban from the face it 'beneath its folds' refers to, or moves the hands before the rest of the body is described, breaks the descending physical sequence.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: Priya had worked as a clerk in the district court for eleven years, and in all that time she had never once arrived late.

A. After a quick breakfast of tea and toast, she walked the same route to the court each day, rain or shine.

B. Yet beneath this rigid routine lay a quiet kindness, for she never refused a junior clerk who came to her in confusion.

C. Once at her desk, she arranged her files by colour before touching a single paper, a habit her colleagues found odd but harmless.

D. Every morning she woke at five o'clock precisely, without needing an alarm, for her body had long since learned the hour.

S2: It was this rare mixture of discipline and warmth that made everyone, from the judge to the sweeper, trust her completely.
solution_text:
The correct answer is D, A, C, B.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A chronological account of Priya's daily routine that ends with a contrasting personality trait.

• D (continues directly from S1's mention of never being late, describing how her morning begins at five o'clock) → A ('After a quick breakfast' follows sequentially from waking in D, describing her walk to court) → C ('Once at her desk' marks her arrival at court, continuing the chronology after A's walk) → B ('Yet' introduces a contrast to the rigid routine just described, revealing her kindness and leading into S2's summary)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Habit-based passages usually follow the clock — 'every morning', 'after', 'once at' — so track the time markers to fix the order before hunting for a final contrast sentence.

 

NOTE

• Placing the kindness sentence (B) before the routine it contrasts with, or breaking the wake-breakfast-desk chronology, leaves the 'yet' with nothing to contrast against.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: As a boy, Arun was so afraid of water that he would not even step near the village pond.

A. Thrashing wildly, he somehow kept his head above the surface until his cousin managed to pull him to the bank.

B. Halfway across, the plank shook beneath him, and Arun slipped, plunging into the rushing water below.

C. Instead of running home in terror, however, Arun found himself strangely calm, and asked his cousin to teach him to swim the very next day.

D. One monsoon evening, his elder cousin dared him to cross the swollen stream on a narrow plank bridge.

S2: Within two years, he was the fastest swimmer in the district, and no one who watched him glide through the water believed the story of his childhood fear.
solution_text:
The correct answer is D, B, A, C.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A single turning-point incident told in strict chronological and cause-effect order.

• D (follows S1 by introducing the specific event — the cousin's dare — that overturns Arun's fear of water) → B ('Halfway across' continues directly from the dare in D, describing the fall into the stream) → A (describes the immediate consequence of the fall in B, ending with the cousin pulling him out) → C ('Instead of running home in terror, however' contrasts with the expected reaction, showing his surprising calm and leading into S2's mention of his skill)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• For turning-point passages, follow the cause-and-effect chain — dare, fall, rescue, reaction — since each event is the direct consequence of the one before it.

 

NOTE

• Swapping the fall (B) and the rescue (A), or moving the calm reaction (C) before the fall, breaks the physical cause-and-effect sequence of the incident.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: Grandmother Kamla was known throughout the fishing village long before anyone could recall exactly how old she was.

A. Around her neck hung a single strand of black beads, said to have been a gift from her long-dead husband.

B. Her sari, a faded indigo with a border worn thin from years of washing, was wrapped in the plain style of the fisherfolk women.

C. Yet it was her eyes, sharp and bright as a girl's despite her ninety-odd years, that people remembered most of all.

D. Her silver hair, always oiled and combed back tightly, was knotted into a small bun no bigger than a lime.

S2: Even the youngest boatmen would fall silent and lower their gaze when those eyes settled upon them.
solution_text:
The correct answer is D, A, B, C.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A head-to-toe physical description that climaxes with the feature people remembered most.

• D (opens the description right after S1 introduces Kamla, starting with her hair, the topmost feature) → A ('Around her neck' moves the description downward from the hair in D to the beads) → B (continues the downward sweep from the neck in A to her sari and general dress) → C ('Yet' breaks from mere clothing to name her eyes as the feature people remembered most, leading directly into S2's mention of 'those eyes')

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• When a description moves from hair to neck to clothing before naming a single striking feature, expect a contrast word like 'yet' or 'but' to mark the climactic final sentence.

 

NOTE

• Placing the eyes (C) before the rest of the appearance is described removes the contrast 'yet' depends on, and separates the neck detail (A) from the hair (D) it follows.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: The retired schoolteacher who lived at the end of Lane Number Four was known to everyone simply as Masterji.

A. Children passing by often lingered near his gate, for he kept a tin of boiled sweets hidden behind a flowerpot for them.

B. Each evening at exactly five o'clock, he would sit on his veranda with a cup of black tea and a newspaper three days old.

C. None of the parents knew about this small secret, and Masterji preferred to keep it that way.

D. He read every article without exception, muttering his disagreement with the editorials under his breath.

S2: Long after he was gone, the flowerpot remained, and every child in the lane still called it "Masterji's tin."
solution_text:
The correct answer is B, D, A, C.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A description of Masterji's evening habits that ends by revealing a secret kindness.

• B (follows S1 by establishing his fixed evening routine of tea and a newspaper) → D (continues the newspaper habit named in B, describing exactly how he read it) → A (shifts to a new, related habit — the hidden tin of sweets — introducing the children who linger near his gate) → C ('this small secret' refers directly to the hidden tin described in A, leading into S2's mention of the flowerpot)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Watch for a phrase like 'this small secret' — it can only follow the sentence that actually reveals the secret, which fixes the order.

 

NOTE

• Placing C before A leaves 'this small secret' with nothing to refer to, and separating B from D breaks the description of a single evening habit.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: Meena was the quietest student in her class, and for two years she had never once raised her hand to answer a question.

A. No one else knew the answer, and after a long silence, Meena slowly raised her trembling hand.

B. The teacher praised her so warmly that the entire class turned to look at her with new respect.

C. One afternoon, the teacher asked who could explain why the classroom lights had suddenly gone out during the storm.

D. She explained, in a voice barely above a whisper, that the transformer near the school often tripped during heavy rain.

S2: From that day, Meena spoke up in class more often, though her voice never quite lost its quiet, careful edge.
solution_text:
The correct answer is C, A, D, B.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A single classroom incident that marks a turning point in a shy student's confidence.

• C (follows S1 with the specific event — a question about the storm — that will break Meena's two-year silence) → A ('No one else knew the answer' responds directly to the question posed in C, leading to Meena raising her hand) → D ('She explained' follows naturally from Meena raising her hand in A, giving the actual answer) → B (describes the teacher's reaction to the explanation given in D, leading into S2's mention of Meena speaking up more often)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• In classroom turning-point passages, trace the question-and-answer sequence — the question, the response, the explanation, the reaction — as each sentence answers the one before it.

 

NOTE

• Placing the explanation (D) before Meena even raises her hand (A), or the praise (B) before she has answered, reverses the natural question-answer-reaction order.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: The shopkeeper at the corner of Market Street had a reputation for honesty that stretched back three generations.

A. He remembered the labourer's torn shirt-pocket and the address near the old well that the man had once mentioned in passing.

B. Without a moment's hesitation, he locked the shop and set off through the dark lanes to find the man's house.

C. That night, while closing the shop, the shopkeeper found fifty rupees still lying untouched in the change drawer.

D. One busy evening, a tired labourer paid for a sack of rice with a hundred-rupee note and rushed off before his change could be counted out.

S2: When he finally placed the fifty rupees in the labourer's astonished hands, he simply said that it was never his to keep.
solution_text:
The correct answer is D, C, A, B.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A single incident illustrating the shopkeeper's honesty, told in strict chronological order.

• D (follows S1 by introducing the specific transaction — the labourer's hurried payment — that sets up the incident) → C ('That night' moves forward in time from D, describing when the untouched change was discovered) → A (explains how the shopkeeper identified whose money it was, recalling details connected to the labourer named in D and C) → B ('Without a moment's hesitation' follows the recognition in A, describing his immediate action, leading into S2's account of returning the money)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Time markers like 'one evening' and 'that night' anchor the order in incident-based passages — list them out to see which event must precede which.

 

NOTE

• Reversing C and A breaks the link between discovering the money and recognising whose it was, and moving B earlier has him act before he even knows where to go.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: The postman who cycled through our lane each morning was, in his own quiet way, something of a local celebrity.

A. Upon his head sat a khaki cap, tilted at an angle that suggested more confidence than the job required.

B. A khaki uniform, pressed each night by his own hand, never showed a single crease by the time he reached our gate.

C. His moustache, waxed and curled at the ends, was the pride of his existence and the envy of younger postmen.

D. His bicycle bell, polished to a shine, announced his arrival long before his face came into view.

S2: Long before we saw him, we would hear that bell and know that the day's letters had arrived.
solution_text:
The correct answer is A, C, B, D.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A head-to-toe physical description that closes on the detail carried into the final sentence.

• A (opens the description right after S1 introduces the postman, starting at the top with his cap) → C (moves the description downward from the cap in A to his moustache) → B (continues downward from the face in C to his uniform) → D (shifts to the bicycle bell, whose sound is echoed directly in S2's 'we would hear that bell')

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• In appearance-based passages, check which sentence's final image is picked up again in S2 — that sentence must come last.

 

NOTE

• Moving the bell (D) earlier severs the direct link between it and S2's repetition of 'that bell', and swapping the cap and moustache reverses the top-down order.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: The night watchman of the old warehouse was famous in the neighbourhood for his elaborate rituals before every shift.

A. He then walked the entire perimeter of the warehouse twice, though a single round would have done just as well.

B. Before switching on his torch, he would touch the gate three times and mutter a short prayer under his breath.

C. Only after these rituals were complete would he finally settle into his chair and open his tattered detective novel.

D. If a dog barked from the left side during his rounds, he considered it a bad sign and delayed his tea break.

S2: Strange as his habits seemed, in eleven years not a single item had ever gone missing from the warehouse under his watch.
solution_text:
The correct answer is B, A, D, C.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A chronological list of the watchman's superstitious rituals from the start of his shift to its settled routine.

• B (follows S1 by describing the very first ritual, performed before the torch is even switched on) → A ('He then walked' follows sequentially from the gate ritual in B, describing his patrol) → D (describes an event that occurs 'during his rounds' named in A, adding a further superstition) → C ('Only after these rituals were complete' sums up everything before it and marks the final settling into his chair, leading into S2's verdict on his habits)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Look for a summarising phrase like 'only after these rituals' — it must come after every ritual it refers to, which fixes it as the final sentence.

 

NOTE

• Placing C before all the rituals it summarises makes no sense, and separating A's patrol from the gate ritual in B breaks the sequence of a single shift's opening routine.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1: In a family where no girl had ever studied past the age of ten, Sunita's father was expected to withdraw her from school the day she turned eleven.

A. Finally, he folded the withdrawal papers into his pocket and told Sunita to be ready for school the next morning.

B. Her father stared at the notebooks for a long time, saying nothing, while the teacher waited patiently beside him.

C. The morning he was to sign the withdrawal papers, Sunita's teacher visited their house unannounced.

D. She spread out Sunita's notebooks on the floor, each page filled with sums solved without a single error.

S2: Years later, Sunita would say that those few silent minutes had decided the entire course of her life.
solution_text:
The correct answer is C, D, B, A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A single turning-point incident in which a silent visit changes a father's decision, told in chronological order.

• C (follows S1 by naming the specific day and the unannounced visit that interrupts the expected withdrawal) → D ('She' refers to the teacher named in C, who spreads out the notebooks as her wordless argument) → B (describes the father's reaction to the notebooks just shown in D, staring in silence) → A ('Finally' marks the resolution of the silence described in B, as the father changes his decision, leading into S2's reflection on those minutes)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• In turning-point passages built on a single scene, track who is doing the acting in each sentence — the pronoun 'she' or 'he' must match the person just introduced.

 

NOTE

• Placing A before the father has even reacted to the notebooks skips the deciding moment, and separating C from D breaks the link between the teacher's arrival and her wordless proof.
